title: Normalized units-sequence Picard boundaries and ideal coefficient maps
statement: Use algebraic spaces and module sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], normalized first-order-thickening site models T for i:X to Xprime [def-sfb-space-square-zero-extension-data], and their square-zero ideal presentations I [def-sfb-space-square-zero-stalk-data]. Restrict the additive ideal to the existing small affine model through the abelian restriction of [def-sfb-space-picard-abelian-pullback]. Restrict the thickened commutative structure sheaf through T inverse and then the affine inclusion. A normalized units-sequence presentation E consists of maps from this additive ideal to the units of the thickened ring and then to the units of the reduced structure ring, with zero composite and sheaf short exactness. On every affine chart the inclusion has unit value 1+I(m), and projection has value the actual quotient applied to the unit value. With any normalized Picard comparison c [def-sfb-ringed-site-picard-data], define its obstruction homomorphism on the existing Picard quotient as c followed by Yoneda postcomposition with E's extension class, from H1 of units to H2 of the additive ideal. For a commuting square of two thickenings, define the predicate on an additive inverse-image ideal map by requiring that, on every compatible pair of reduced affine charts and their lifted chart map over the thickened-space morphism, composing the ideal inclusion with its action on each local unit-image section equals pullback of the original ideal section as a regular function. Define the predicate on a tensor-pullback ideal map [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] by the analogous formula on every local tensor a tensor m: after ideal inclusion its value is r times the pulled-back ideal section, for every lift r of a in the thickened ring. These are predicates fixing the maps by chart formulas, with no existence assertion. The ordinary pullback on the small model is the existing conjugated tensor functor [def-sfb-space-derived-tensor-pullback].
